findings.description: AWS access key and secret access key are embedded in plaintext within the EC2 user_data script, which is stored in Terraform state and accessible via the EC2 instance metadata service/console to anyone with access to the instance, leading to credential leakage.

The EBS volume does not set encrypted = true (the setting is even commented out), meaning data at rest on the volume is stored unencrypted, exposing it to disclosure if the underlying storage or a snapshot is compromised.
The snapshot is created from an unencrypted EBS volume and has no encryption configured, so any snapshot data (and copies/shares of it) remains unencrypted at rest.

The security group allows inbound SSH (port 22) from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing the management port to the entire internet and enabling brute-force or credential-based attacks against the host, which also resides in a public subnet.
The security group allows inbound HTTP (port 80) from 0.0.0.0/0 with no compensating controls, broadening the attack surface for the exposed web service.
The egress rule allows all traffic (protocol -1, all ports) to 0.0.0.0/0, which combined with public ingress increases the risk of data exfiltration if the instance is compromised.

map_public_ip_on_launch = true automatically assigns public IP addresses to instances launched in this subnet; combined with the internet gateway route and the permissive security group, this directly exposes the web_host instance (including its SSH port) to the public internet.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true automatically assigns public IP addresses to any instance launched in this subnet, unnecessarily exposing future workloads to the public internet.

findings.issue_category: missing encryption and public access controls
findings.description: The S3 bucket used to store VPC flow logs has no server-side encryption configuration and no public access block or bucket policy restricting access, risking unauthorized access to and disclosure of network flow log data.
